body:
This feels really odd to me. I think it'd make more sense if `RenderingDevice` got a function that returns the MSAA levels supported for a data format, and the internal implementations of `viewport_set_msaa_2d`/`viewport_set_msaa_3d` snapped `RSE::ViewportMSAA` to the nearest level on its own. This'd also fairly decrease the git diff.

For example, for 3D, I'd do this snapping inside `RenderSceneBuffers::configure` where `msaa_3d` gets assigned.
Done!
Oof, I forgot we use two different enums for MSAA. This makes things not quite as nice as @blueskythlikesclouds envisioned
The same changes will be needed for 2D MSAA.

I think Skyth's suggestion was to actually validate MSAA here: 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/75e2933fcece578c97de58b61652d31c58f43428/servers/rendering/renderer_viewport.cpp#L168
Doh, good catch
yeah, have to keep converting between the two
And by validate, does that mean return an error if it isn't supported?

No, sorry. By validate I meant replace the passed in value with an actual supported value. Which is what you are doing here. I misread Skyth's comment, I thought he wanted to call this as soon as possible. But this actually is what he suggested.

I have no preference between calling this here, or calling it in RendererViewport. As long as we consistently have access to the same value throughout the renderer internally. 

So no need to change anything on this point
It now also handles 2D MSAA
What's with this refactor? Doesn't seem relevant to the PR.
Yeah, sorry – thought it was a little clearer to move to a clearly-named function, but in hindsight, not so much. I've removed it.

Color also probably should be checked here. Then we can take the minimum one.

Edit: Oh I see why you didn't add color, the data format is tied to an instanced object, the function is not static. That's tricky... I guess we could stick to depth for now as long as it fixes the problem on devices where we know it's a problem.
Yeah, I think this is all necessary for D3D12. Both Metal and Vulkan are not tied to the texture format.
Is the supported sample count different on any platforms between RGBA16 and RGB10_A2? I suspect we can just always check against RGBA16 and whatever depth format this returns

That sounds reasonable. 

It won't be different for Vulkan and Metal, because both just report a limit / capability check and ignore the texture format.

I'd be interested in @blueskythlikesclouds' thoughts from a D3D12 perspective.

[From the D3D11 spec](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/archive/D3D11_3_FunctionalSpec.htm):

> D3D11 requires support for 1x(trivial), 4x and 8x MSAA, with at minimum support for the standard patterns for these MSAA counts. At 4x MSAA, all output (RenderTarget/DepthStencil-able) formats must be supported. At 8x MSAA, only output formats with less than 128 bits per sample must be supported. Support for 128+ bits per sample formats with 8x MSAA is optional. Other MSAA counts and patterns are optional as before.

Looks like 4x and 8x are pretty much guaranteed in D3D12, while 2x can be optional.

In practice though I think we'd be hard pressed to find any GPU that does not support 2x MSAA on D3D12.

I noticed another thing: the D3D12 code actually seems to be broken? If 4x/8x are supported but 2x isn't, and an attempt to create a 2x texture is made, it won't round it down to 1x, since it does `min(max supported sample count, requested sample count)`
I'll verify that now

You're right. I looked further and found two existing bugs in the D3D12 sample-count logic. This PR copies both into `texture_get_nearest_supported_samples`, because I kept the old texture_create logic as it was. 

Worth noting that `_find_max_common_supported_sample_count` returns twice the actual value, as nearest_shift adds 1:

```cpp
return ((uint32_t)1 << Math::nearest_shift(common));
```

So if common is `8`, the result is `16`:

```cpp
return 1 << 4
```
@blueskythlikesclouds this should be fixed now
